abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Following a request from the European Commission, EFSA was asked to deliver a scientific opinion on the safety and efficacy of vitamin B1 (thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate) for the renewal of its authorisation as nutritional feed additive for all animal species. The Panel on Additives and Products or Substances used in Animal Feed (FEEDAP) concluded that vitamin B1 remains safe for all animal species, consumers and the environment. Thiamine mononitrate is not irritant to the eyes, while hydrochloride is not irritant to skin, but it is irritant to the eyes. Both salts of thiamine are considered skin and respiratory sensitisers, and any exposure is considered a risk. These conclusions would apply, in principle, to any preparations produced with the thiamine mononitrate. The Panel concluded there is no need for assessing the efficacy of the additive in the context of the renewal of the authorisation.

sec.p: Keywords: efficacy, nutritional additives, safety, thiamine hydrochloride, thiamine mononitrate, vitamin B1
Collection date 2025 Apr.

sec.title: Background and Terms of Reference
sec.p: Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 1 establishes the rules governing the Community authorisation of additives for use in animal nutrition. In particular, Article 14(1) of that Regulation lays down that an application for renewal shall be sent to the Commission at the latest 1 year before the expiry date of the authorisation.

The European Commission received a request from DSM Nutritional Products Ltd. represented in the EU by DSM Nutritional Products Sp. z o.o., and Orffa Additives BV 2 for the renewal of the authorisation of vitamin B1 as thiamine hydrochloride (3a820) and thiamine mononitrate (3a821), when used as feed additives for all animal species and categories (category: nutritional additives; functional group: vitamins, pro‐vitamins and chemically well‐defined substances having similar effect).

According to Article 7(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003, the Commission forwarded the application to the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) as an application under Article 14(1) (renewal of the authorisation). The dossier was received on 19 June 2024 and the general information and supporting documentation are available at https://open.efsa.europa.eu/questions/EFSA‐Q‐2024‐00407. The particulars and documents in support of the application were considered valid by EFSA as of 22 August 2024.

sec.title: Additional information
sec.p: Vitamin B1 is currently authorised in the form of thiamine hydrochloride (3a820) and thiamine mononitrate (3a821) as nutritional additives for use in feed and in water for drinking for all animal species. 3 Thiamine hydrochloride is also authorised as a flavouring compound in feed for all animal species (2b16027). 4

EFSA issued three opinions on the safety and efficacy of vitamin B1 as thiamine mononitrate and as thiamine hydrochloride when used in feed for all animal species (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2011a, 2011b, 2011c).

sec.title: Data
sec.p: The present assessment is based on data submitted by the applicants in the form of a technical dossier 5 in support of the authorisation request for the use of vitamin B1 as thiamine hydrochloride (3a820) and thiamine mononitrate (3a821) as a feed additive.

In accordance with Article 38 of the Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 6 and taking into account the protection of confidential information and of personal data in accordance with Articles 39 to 39e of the same Regulation, and of the Decision of EFSA's Executive Director laying down practical arrangements concerning transparency and confidentiality, 7 a non‐confidential version of the dossier has been published on Open.EFSA.

According to Article 32c(2) of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and to the Decision of EFSA's Executive Director laying down the practical arrangements on pre‐submission phase and public consultations, EFSA carried out a public consultation on the non‐confidential version of the technical dossier from 3 January to 24 January 2025 for which no comments were received.

The confidential version of the technical dossier was subject to a target consultation of the interested Member States from 26 August 2024 to 26 November 2024; the comments received were considered for the assessment.

The FEEDAP Panel used the data provided by the applicant together with data from other sources, such as previous risk assessments by EFSA or other expert bodies, peer‐reviewed scientific papers, other scientific reports and experts' (elicitation) knowledge, to deliver the present output.

The European Union Reference Laboratory (EURL) considered that the conclusions and recommendations reached in the previous assessment regarding the methods used for the control of thiamine mononitrate and thiamine hydrochloride in animal feed are valid and applicable for the current application. 8

sec.title: Methodologies
sec.p: The approach followed by the FEEDAP Panel to assess the safety and the efficacy of vitamin B1 as thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate is in line with the principles laid down in Regulation (EC) No 429/2008 9 and the relevant guidance documents: Guidance on the renewal of the authorisation of feed additives (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2021).

sec.title: ASSESSMENT
sec.p: Vitamin B1 is currently authorised in the form of thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate as nutritional additives for use in feed and water for drinking for all animal species. The present application is for the renewal of the above authorisation.
The data supporting the application for thiamine hydrochloride was generated by one company while that for thiamine mononitrate by two companies.

sec.title: Characterisation
sec.p: Thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate are produced by chemical synthesis, and they appear as white or almost white to pale yellow crystalline powders or small crystals. Thiamine hydrochloride is used as such while thiamine mononitrate may be used in the form of a preparation. 10

sec.title: Thiamine hydrochloride
sec.p: Thiamine hydrochloride (IUPAC name 3‐[(4‐amino‐2‐methylpyrimidin‐5‐yl)methyl]‐5‐(2‐hydroxyethyl)‐4‐methylthiazolium chloride hydrochloride) has the EINECS number 200‐641‐8, the CAS number 67‐03‐8, a molecular formula C12H17N4OS + Cl−•HCl and a molecular mass of 337.3 g/mol.
Thiamine hydrochloride is currently authorised with a minimum purity of 98.5% on anhydrous basis.

The applicant stated that the manufacturing process remained unchanged since the previous authorisation. 11 The applicant submitted data on the batch‐to‐batch variation and impurities which are reported in Table 1. 12 Considering that the composition and the manufacturing of the additive has not been modified, the data on the physico‐chemical properties already evaluated in the previous opinions are considered to still apply (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2011a, 2011c). However, the applicant provided data on the stability of thiamine hydrochloride in liquid vitamin premixtures which are also reported in Table 1.

sec.p: The data provided by the applicant confirmed compliance with the specifications set by the authorisation Regulation (EU) No 2015/897. The Panel notes that the levels of the substance‐related impurities comply with the limits of the PhEur (European Pharmacopoeia (PhEur), 2025a) and those of residual solvents are below the limits set by VICH (EMA, 2023). The FEEDAP Panel considers that the amounts of the detected impurities do not raise safety concerns.

sec.title: Thiamine mononitrate
sec.p: Thiamine mononitrate (IUPAC name 3‐[(4‐amino‐2‐methylpyrimidin‐5‐yl)methyl]‐5‐(2‐hydroxyethyl)‐4‐methylthiazolium nitrate) has the EINECS number 208‐537‐4, the CAS number 532‐43‐4, a molecular formula C12H17N4OS·NO3 and a molecular mass of 327.36 g/mol.
Thiamine mononitrate is currently authorised with a minimum purity of 98% on anhydrous basis.

One of the applicants states that the manufacturing processes remained unchanged11 since the previous authorisation, while the other states that solvents are not used anymore in the manufacturing process. The FEEDAP Panel considers that these changes do not have an impact on the composition and properties of the additive. The applicant submitted data on the batch‐to‐batch variation 13 and impurities 14 which are reported in Table 2. Considering that no significant changes have been introduced in the manufacturing process and composition of the active substance, the data described in the previous opinion regarding physico‐chemical properties (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2011a, 2011b) are still valid.

sec.p: The data provided by the applicants confirmed compliance with the specifications set by the authorisation Regulation (EU) No 2015/897. The Panel notes that the levels of the substance‐related impurities comply with the limits of the PhEur (European Pharmacopoeia (PhEur), 2025b) and those of residual solvents are below the limits set by VICH (2023). The FEEDAP Panel considers that the amounts of the detected impurities do not raise safety concerns.

The current authorisation states that thiamine mononitrate may be placed on the market and used as an additive consisting of a preparation. The applicants stated that they do not produce preparations of thiamine mononitrate.

sec.title: Conditions of use
sec.p: Thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate are authorised for use in feed for all animal species and categories without a minimum or maximum content.
Under other provisions of the two authorisations, it is stated the following.

list-item.p: In the directions for use of the additive and premixture, indicate the storage and the stability conditions.
Thiamine hydrochloride/thiamine mononitrate may be used via water for drinking.
For safety: breathing protection, safety glasses and gloves shall be worn during handling.

sec.p: In addition, for thiamine mononitrate:

list-item.p: Thiamine mononitrate may be placed on the market and used as an additive consisting of a preparation.

sec.p: The applicant did not request any change in the current conditions of the authorisation.

sec.title: Safety
sec.p: The safety of vitamin B1 in the form of thiamine mononitrate and thiamine hydrochloride was evaluated in previous opinions (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2011a, 2011b, 2011c). The FEEDAP Panel concluded that the additives were safe for the target animals, for the consumers and for the environment. Regarding user safety, the Panel concluded that both thiamine salts were regarded as skin and eye irritants, and skin and respiratory sensitisers.

The applicants declared that no safety issues for target animals, consumers, users and/or the environment have been documented or reported regarding the additives since their previous authorisation. 15

sec.title: Extensive literature search
sec.p: The applicants performed an extensive literature search (ELS) 16 to provide evidence that the additive remains safe under the approved conditions for the target species, consumers, users and the environment. The literature search covered the period 2010 to 2023 using three database platforms and 13 additional databases. 17 The search protocol described the inclusion and exclusion criteria applied for the screening process. A total of 345 hits were considered for the screening and after applying the exclusion criteria, a total of 14 hits were considered eligible and relevant by the applicant for the safety of additive. The FEEDAP Panel reviewed the papers and considered that none of them provides information that would modify the conclusions previously reached with regards the safety for the target species, consumers and the environment.

sec.title: Safety for the user
sec.p: Regarding user safety, the applicants provided new studies on the skin/eye irritation and skin sensitisation potential which are described below. In addition, the literature search retrieved two papers reporting one case of contact dermatitis for thiamine hydrochloride and another case of skin sensitisation for an unspecified form of thiamine (Arruti et al., 2013; Rodríguez‐Fernández et al., 2018). 18

The skin irritation potential of thiamine hydrochloride was tested in a study performed according to OECD Testing Guideline (TG) 439, 19 which showed that the additive is not a skin irritant (UN GHS No Category).

The eye irritation potential of thiamine hydrochloride was tested in two studies performed according to OECD TGs 437 20 and 492. 21 The results of the test performed according to the OECD TG 437 showed that no standalone predictions can be made while the results of the OECD TG 492 showed that thiamine hydrochloride is not an eye irritant for 50% solutions or below, but the neat active substance is an eye irritant (UN GHS Category 1 or Category 2).
The eye irritation potential of thiamine mononitrate was tested in a study performed according to OECD TG 437 22 which showed that thiamine mononitrate is not an eye irritant (UN GHS No Category).

The skin sensitisation potential of thiamine hydrochloride was tested in three studies performed according to OECD TG 442C, 23 442D 24 and 442E. 25 The results of the 442C test placed thiamine hydrochloride in the positive result category for the ‘low reactivity class’, whereas the results of the 442D and 442E tests were negative.

Considering the results of the skin sensitisation test together with the known sensitising properties of thiamine, supported by the findings in the ELS and in the previous opinions (EFSA FEEDAP Panel, 2011a, 2011b, 2011c), the FEEDAP Panel considers that both forms of thiamine should be considered as skin and respiratory sensitisers.

sec.title: Conclusions on the safety
sec.p: Considering all the above, the FEEDAP Panel concludes that thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate remain safe for the target species, consumers and the environment under the conditions of the authorisation. Thiamine mononitrate is not irritant to the eyes, while hydrochloride is not irritant to skin, but it is irritant to the eyes. Both salts of thiamine are considered skin and respiratory sensitisers, and any dermal and inhalation exposure is considered a risk. These conclusions would apply, in principle, to any preparations produced with the thiamine mononitrate.

sec.title: Efficacy
sec.p: The present application for renewal of the authorisation does not include a proposal for amending or supplementing the conditions of the original authorisation that would have an impact on the efficacy of the additive. Therefore, there is no need for assessing the efficacy of the additive in the context of the renewal of the authorisation.

sec.title: Post‐market monitoring
sec.p: The FEEDAP Panel considers that there is no need for specific requirements for a post‐market monitoring plan other than those established in the Feed Hygiene Regulation 26 and Good Manufacturing Practice.

sec.title: CONCLUSIONS
sec.p: The applicant provided evidence that the additives currently in the market comply with the conditions of the authorisation.
The use of thiamine hydrochloride and thiamine mononitrate in animal nutrition remains safe for the target species, the consumers and the environment under the approved conditions of use.

Regarding user safety, the FEEDAP Panel concludes that thiamine mononitrate is not irritant to the eyes, while hydrochloride is not irritant to skin, but it is irritant to the eyes. Both salts of thiamine are considered skin and respiratory sensitisers, and any dermal and respiratory exposure is considered a risk. These conclusions would apply, in principle, to any preparations produced with the thiamine mononitrate.
There is no need to assess the efficacy of the additive in the context of the renewal of the authorisation.
